issues.legal_issue: A civil court’s jurisdiction to decide an inheritance-based title claim is not barred when the claim arises after the consolidation scheme has been finalized and implemented and the claim cannot be brought under the consolidation statute.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a civil suit for partition, claiming a share as the son of a person who had predeceased the property owner.
The consolidation scheme concerning the property had been finalized and published while the property owner was alive, and the scheme had been implemented so that possession was delivered.
The property owner died after those consolidation operations, giving rise to the inheritance claim.
The consolidation statute provided no procedure for deciding a title dispute arising after confirmation of the scheme; subsequent revenue records were governed by land-revenue law.
issues.conclusion: The civil court’s jurisdiction was not barred, and it could investigate and adjudicate the disputed title and sonship. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: An exclusion of civil-court jurisdiction must be strictly construed. The first limb of Section 49 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953 applies to matters directly connected with and arising out of consolidation proceedings, not matters merely arising during them. Its second limb applies only to matters for which a suit or application could be filed under that Act. Where an inheritance claim arises after the scheme has been finalized and implemented and the Act supplies no procedure for that later claim, neither limb bars a civil suit. Sections 23 and 27(1), (3) of the Act, read with Sections 33 and 48 of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901, support that distinction. The Court approved the reasoning in Shrimati Natho v. Board of Revenue, U.P. and Smt. Bhuri v. Sunder, insofar as consistent with its analysis.

predicates.civil_partition_or_title_suit: A person brought a civil suit seeking partition or determination of title to property.
predicates.inheritance_claim_arose_after_scheme_fin: The event giving rise to the inheritance claim occurred after the consolidation scheme had been finalized.
predicates.consolidation_substantially_completed_fo: The scheme had been implemented for the property, including the allotment or delivery of possession, before the later claim arose.
predicates.later_claim_outside_consolidation_remedi: The consolidation statute provided no procedure for bringing or deciding the claim that arose after the scheme was finalized.

issues.definition: When a civil partition or title suit concerns an inheritance claim arising after the scheme has been finalized and substantially implemented, and the later claim falls outside the available consolidation remedies, a civil court may adjudicate title.
